AccountDeletionPlanRead.description:
What deleting the caller's account would do to each workspace they are in.

`blocking` workspaces stop the deletion: the caller is their only owner and
other people are in them, so ownership has to move or the workspace has to be
deleted first. One already scheduled for deletion carries `deletion_scheduled`
and stops blocking once its own purge starts. `deleted_with_account` have no other members. `leaving` keep
going without the caller.
AccountDeletionPlanRead.title: AccountDeletionPlanRead

AccountDeletionRequest.description: The body `POST /api/users/me/deletion` takes: the account's address typed out again.
AccountDeletionRequest.title: AccountDeletionRequest

ActivityRead.description:
One activity row as the API returns it.

`from` and `to` are the wire names the contract fixes, and `from` is a Python
keyword, so both are aliased off the stored `from_value` and `to_value`.
ActivityRead.title: ActivityRead

ApiKeyCreated.description:
The one response that carries the plaintext key.

There is no route that shows `secret` again and no support path that can
recover it, because the stored row holds only a SHA-256 of it. A lost key is
revoked and reminted.
ApiKeyCreated.title: ApiKeyCreated

ApiKeyListRead.description: The list envelope, one plural key, per the contract's list shape.
ApiKeyListRead.title: ApiKeyListRead

ApiKeyRead.description: One stored key as a listing renders it. Carries no credential.
ApiKeyRead.title: ApiKeyRead

ArchiveSettingsRead.description: A team's auto-archive setting as the API returns it.
ArchiveSettingsRead.title: ArchiveSettingsRead

ArchiveSettingsUpdate.description:
The body a team's auto-archive settings patch takes.

`period_months` is how long after an issue was completed or cancelled it is
archived, one of Linear's own choices.
ArchiveSettingsUpdate.title: ArchiveSettingsUpdate

AttachmentRead.description:
One attachment as the API returns it.

`s3_key` is returned so the frontend can key a cache on it. It is not a
credential: the bucket is private and the only way to a byte is the download
route, which mints a presigned GET per request.
AttachmentRead.title: AttachmentRead

AuthorRead.description:
Who wrote a comment, denormalised onto the response.

Rendered from one batched user read per page rather than stored on the row, so
a display name change is reflected without rewriting every comment.
AuthorRead.title: AuthorRead

BillingRead.description: A workspace's plan, subscription and the ceilings and features that plan grants.
BillingRead.title: BillingRead

BillingSessionRead.description: A hosted Stripe page the browser is sent to.
BillingSessionRead.title: BillingSessionRead

BoardColumn.description: One board column: a status, the issues in it, and how to read more.
BoardColumn.title: BoardColumn

BoardRead.description: A whole board: one column per status of the team, in position order.
BoardRead.title: BoardRead

CarryOverRead.description: What cycle closes moved into and out of one cycle, in issues and in points.
CarryOverRead.title: CarryOverRead

CheckoutCreate.description: The plan and billing interval a Checkout Session is started for.
CheckoutCreate.title: CheckoutCreate

CommentCreate.description:
The body a comment create takes.

`attachment_ids` names attachments already on the same issue, uploaded or
linked first through the attachment routes, which the comment then shows
inline. The route holds that each one exists under this issue. The body may
be empty only when the comment carries an attachment, so a screenshot can be
posted without a caption while a comment is never blank.
CommentCreate.title: CommentCreate

CommentRead.description: One comment as the API returns it.
CommentRead.title: CommentRead

CommentUpdate.description: The body a comment edit takes, carrying the issue that partitions it.
CommentUpdate.title: CommentUpdate

ConnectedAppListRead.description: The caller's connected apps, most recently used first.
ConnectedAppListRead.title: ConnectedAppListRead

ConnectedAppMemberRead.description: The person who authorized a client, as a workspace admin sees them.
ConnectedAppMemberRead.title: ConnectedAppMemberRead

ConnectedAppRead.description: One client the caller authorized, across every workspace they granted it.
ConnectedAppRead.title: ConnectedAppRead

ConnectedAppWorkspaceRead.description: One workspace a client was authorized in, and what it may do there.
ConnectedAppWorkspaceRead.title: ConnectedAppWorkspaceRead

ConversionRequest.description: The `code` and `state` GitHub sent the browser back with.
ConversionRequest.title: ConversionRequest

CountsRead.description:
One planning row's issue counts as the API returns them.

`total` is rendered rather than stored so a reader never has to trust that the
four buckets agree with a fifth counter that could drift from them.
CountsRead.title: CountsRead

CreatedApp.description:
The new App as the admin may see it, and where to finish its setup.

Only the id and slug: the private key, client secret and webhook secret went
straight into the `app` secret and are never answered.
CreatedApp.title: CreatedApp

CycleCapacityRead.description: The active or next cycle's current scope, which capacity guidance weighs.
CycleCapacityRead.title: CycleCapacityRead

CycleHistoryPoint.description:
One day of a cycle's burn-up, in issues and in estimate points.

`scope` excludes cancelled work, `started` includes finished work, and
`completed` is finished work alone, matching the cycle page's own figures.
CycleHistoryPoint.title: CycleHistoryPoint

CycleHistoryRead.description: A cycle's daily scope history, first day to today or its end.
CycleHistoryRead.title: CycleHistoryRead

CycleRead.description: One cycle as the API returns it, with its status derived from its dates.
CycleRead.title: CycleRead

CycleSettingsRead.description: A team's automatic cycle settings as the API returns them.
CycleSettingsRead.title: CycleSettingsRead

CycleSettingsUpdate.description:
The body a team's cycle settings patch takes, every field optional.

`start_weekday` counts from Monday as 0 to Sunday as 6.
CycleSettingsUpdate.title: CycleSettingsUpdate

CycleUpdate.description:
The body a cycle patch takes.

`team_id` is required rather than patchable: it names the partition prefix
the row is filed under, and moving a cycle between teams would orphan every
issue pointing at it.
CycleUpdate.title: CycleUpdate

DeliveryAttemptRead.description:
One try at posting a delivery: what came back and how long it took.

`status_code` is 0 when no HTTP response arrived, in which case `error` says why.
DeliveryAttemptRead.title: DeliveryAttemptRead

DownloadRead.description:
A presigned GET and when it stops working.

Minted per request and never stored or logged, so the window is the whole
guard on a URL that is a bearer credential until it expires.
DownloadRead.title: DownloadRead

ErrorResponse.description:
The `"detailed"` error envelope every handler renders, and what OpenAPI advertises.

`details` is present only on a 422, where it holds one entry per offending field.

details.description: Per-field validation failures. Present only on a 422.
details.title: Details

error_code.description: A stable machine readable code, such as `NOT_FOUND`.
error_code.title: Error Code

message.description: A human readable summary safe to surface to a caller.
message.title: Message

request_id.description: The request id, echoed in the `X-Request-ID` header.
request_id.title: Request Id

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body.
status.title: Status

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

GitHubAppStatus.description: Whether this environment can create an App, and whether it already has one.
GitHubAppStatus.title: GitHubAppStatus

IconCommit.description: The body an icon commit takes: the upload id the presign call returned.
IconCommit.title: IconCommit

IconUploadCreate.description: The body an icon presign call takes: the image type and its exact size.
IconUploadCreate.title: IconUploadCreate

IconUploadRead.description: The signed PUT for one icon and the headers it must be sent with.
IconUploadRead.title: IconUploadRead

InboxCountRead.description: The unread badge, counted from the sparse index and capped.
InboxCountRead.title: InboxCountRead

InboxReadRequest.description: The body a mark-read takes: either a list of ids or the whole inbox.
InboxReadRequest.title: InboxReadRequest

InboxReadResult.description: How many notifications a mark-read actually moved.
InboxReadResult.title: InboxReadResult

InboxSnoozeRequest.description:
The body a snooze takes: the ids to hide and the moment they come back.

`until` must carry a timezone, so the moment a notification returns does not
depend on where the server happens to run.
InboxSnoozeRequest.title: InboxSnoozeRequest

InboxUnreadRequest.description: The body a mark-unread takes: the ids to bring back as unread.
InboxUnreadRequest.title: InboxUnreadRequest

InstallUrlRead.description: Where to send a workspace admin to install the GitHub App.
InstallUrlRead.title: InstallUrlRead

InstallationRead.description: The GitHub App installation a workspace has, if any.
InstallationRead.title: InstallationRead

InviteCreate.description:
The body `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/invites` takes.

`owner` is absent from the role type on purpose: ownership is granted to an
existing member, never handed to an unaccepted email address.
InviteCreate.title: InviteCreate

InviteCreated.description:
The 201 body of a created invite, carrying the token exactly once.

Only the hash is stored, so this response is the single moment the token
exists in readable form. Mail delivery is out of M1's scope, which is why the
token is returned to the caller to pass on.
InviteCreated.title: InviteCreated

InviteListRead.description: The body the invites list route answers with.
InviteListRead.title: InviteListRead

InviteRead.description: One invite as the API returns it, carrying no token.
InviteRead.title: InviteRead

IssueBulkPatch.description:
The fields one bulk patch sets on every named issue.

The triage fields only: a title, body or date is per issue by nature, so a bulk
write of one would be a mistake rather than a shortcut. Labels are an add and a
remove rather than a replacement, so tagging a selection keeps each issue's
other labels.

`archived` archives the selection when true and restores it when false, after
any field change in the same patch, so a selection is archived in one request
rather than one per issue.
IssueBulkPatch.title: IssueBulkPatch

IssueBulkRead.description:
What a bulk patch answers with.

`issues` is every named issue after the write, in request order. `skipped`
names any issue deleted between validation and its write: validation is all
or nothing, but the writes are separate puts, and a concurrent delete is the
one failure that can land between them.
IssueBulkRead.title: IssueBulkRead

IssueCreate.description:
The body `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/issues` takes.

`team_id` is a field rather than a path segment because issues are workspace
scoped, which is what lets a link and a "my issues" read cross teams.
IssueCreate.title: IssueCreate

IssueLinkRead.description: One pull request linked to one issue.
IssueLinkRead.title: IssueLinkRead

IssueSyncListRead.description:
The issue list route's body: a page, plus the cursor a polling client resumes from.

`synced_at` is the cursor to send back as `updated_since`. A delta read answers
the changed issues that match under `issues`, the ids to drop from the cached
list under `removed_ids`, and `resync_required` when the client must read the
list in full instead. A full read carries `synced_at` alone, so every existing
caller reads the same body it always did.
IssueSyncListRead.title: IssueSyncListRead

IssueSyncRead.description: The GitHub issue one issue is synced with.
IssueSyncRead.title: IssueSyncRead

IssueUpdate.description:
The body an issue patch takes.

`team_id` is absent by design: the contract makes it unchangeable, and an
issue's key, counter and every index composite are derived from it.
IssueUpdate.title: IssueUpdate

LabelCreate.description: The body a label create takes.
LabelCreate.title: LabelCreate

LabelListRead.description: The body the labels list route answers with.
LabelListRead.title: LabelListRead

LabelRead.description: One label as the API returns it.
LabelRead.title: LabelRead

LabelUpdate.description: The body a label patch takes.
LabelUpdate.title: LabelUpdate

LinkCreate.description: The body a link create takes.
LinkCreate.title: LinkCreate

LinkListRead.description: The body the links list route answers with, both directions together.
LinkListRead.title: LinkListRead

LinkRead.description: One link as the API returns it, joined with the far side for display.
LinkRead.title: LinkRead

LinkStatusRead.description:
The far side's status on a link, so a row can draw its glyph.

Carried on the link because the far side may sit in another team, whose
statuses the page showing this issue never loads.
LinkStatusRead.title: LinkStatusRead

ManifestStart.description: What the page posts to GitHub: the manifest, and the url carrying the signed state.
ManifestStart.title: ManifestStart

MediaTokensRead.description:
Media tokens for the file attachments on one issue, keyed by attachment id.

Each token is appended to that attachment's stable content path at render time,
so a stored body never carries a credential.
MediaTokensRead.title: MediaTokensRead

MemberListRead.description: The body the members list route answers with.
MemberListRead.title: MemberListRead

MemberRead.description: One workspace member, joined with the user row for a renderable identity.
MemberRead.title: MemberRead

MemberUpdate.description: The body a member role change takes.
MemberUpdate.title: MemberUpdate

MilestoneCreate.description:
The body `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/projects/{project_id}/milestones` takes.

`sort_order` is optional: left out, the milestone is placed after the last one.
MilestoneCreate.title: MilestoneCreate

MilestoneRead.description: One project milestone as the API returns it, with its progress counts.
MilestoneRead.title: MilestoneRead

MilestoneUpdate.description:
The body a milestone patch takes; a reorder is a patch of `sort_order` alone.

Setting the description or the target date to null clears it.
MilestoneUpdate.title: MilestoneUpdate

NotificationChannels.description: Where one kind of notification is delivered: the inbox and email.
NotificationChannels.title: NotificationChannels

NotificationChannelsUpdate.description: A partial change to one kind's channels; an omitted channel keeps its value.
NotificationChannelsUpdate.title: NotificationChannelsUpdate

NotificationRead.description:
One inbox row as the API returns it.

A `project_update` notification names its project and update and leaves the
issue fields empty.
NotificationRead.title: NotificationRead

ProgressRead.description: An issue's direct-child rollup as the API returns it.
ProgressRead.title: ProgressRead

ProjectCreate.description:
The body `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/projects` takes.

`team_ids` is the project's teams, at least one. `team_id` is the single-team
spelling an older client sends; given alone it is read as a one-team list, and
given beside `team_ids` it must be one of them.
ProjectCreate.title: ProjectCreate

ProjectRead.description:
One project as the API returns it, with its status stored rather than derived.

`team_ids` holds only the teams the caller can see, so a guest learns nothing
about the rest of the workspace from a shared project. `team_id` is the first
of them, kept for a single-team reader.
ProjectRead.title: ProjectRead

ProjectUpdate.description:
The body a project patch takes.

`team_ids` replaces the teams the caller can see; teams the caller cannot see
are kept as they are, so a guest's edit never drops a team it was never
shown. `team_id` is the single-team spelling an older client sends; it moves
nothing and must name one of the project's teams, or the patch is a 404.
ProjectUpdate.title: ProjectUpdate

ProjectUpdateCreate.description:
The body `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/projects/{project_id}/updates` takes.

Health is required, as in Linear, because an update is the report of how the
project stands and posting one is what sets the project's health.
ProjectUpdateCreate.title: ProjectUpdateCreate

ProjectUpdatePatch.description: The body a project update patch takes; either field may be left out, neither cleared.
ProjectUpdatePatch.title: ProjectUpdatePatch

ProjectUpdateRead.description:
One project update as the API returns it.

`can_edit` says whether this caller may edit or delete it, which is its
author, a workspace admin or an admin of one of the project's teams, so a
client draws the menu without repeating the rule.
ProjectUpdateRead.title: ProjectUpdateRead

ReactionGroupRead.description:
One emoji's reactions on one target.

`reacted` is resolved against the calling user, which is what lets the frontend
render the caller's own reaction as pressed without a second read.
ReactionGroupRead.title: ReactionGroupRead

ReactionListRead.description:
The body the reactions list route answers with.

Not a cursor page: a group is a count over a whole partition, so a page
boundary would produce a count of part of it.
ReactionListRead.title: ReactionListRead

ReactionWrite.description:
The body a reaction `PUT` takes.

`issue_id` is required for a `comment` target and ignored for an `issue` one,
because a comment's partition is its issue and the route reads the comment back
to hold that the pair really goes together.
ReactionWrite.title: ReactionWrite

RepositoryLinkWrite.description: Point one repository at one team, or clear it.
RepositoryLinkWrite.title: RepositoryLinkWrite

RepositoryRead.description: One repository the installation can see.
RepositoryRead.title: RepositoryRead

RoadmapEntryRead.description:
One cycle or project as the roadmap draws it.

A projection rather than the full row: the timeline renders a bar and a count,
and a reader wanting the rest has the entity's own route. The icon, colour,
health and priority are a project's alone, so a cycle answers them as null.
RoadmapEntryRead.title: RoadmapEntryRead

SearchRead.description: Every search hit, ranked. No cursor, per the contract.
SearchRead.title: SearchRead

SearchResultRead.description: One search hit: enough of an issue to render a row, plus its score.
SearchResultRead.title: SearchResultRead

ShareLinkCreate.description:
The body `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/share-links` takes.

An `issue` or `view` link names its row by `target_id`. A `filter` link
publishes an unsaved team filter: `target_id` is the team, and `filter`, `sort`
and `title` are snapshotted onto the link, so what it shows cannot drift from
what the person saw when they published it.
ShareLinkCreate.title: ShareLinkCreate

ShareLinkCreated.description:
The one response that carries the plaintext token.

`url` on this response carries the token, because it is the thing a person
copies. Every other response carries the tokenless path.
ShareLinkCreated.title: ShareLinkCreated

ShareLinkListRead.description: The list envelope, one plural key, per the contract's list shape.
ShareLinkListRead.title: ShareLinkListRead

ShareLinkRead.description:
One share link as the settings list renders it. Carries no live token.

`url` here is the path with no token on it. A list that carried live tokens
would make the list itself a credential, so the token appears only on the
create response.
ShareLinkRead.title: ShareLinkRead

SharedComment.description:
One comment on a shared issue.

`author_name` is a display name and never a user id or an email, so a share
cannot be used to harvest the membership of the workspace it came from.
SharedComment.title: SharedComment

SharedIssue.description:
One shared issue, in full, bounded by the one row the token resolved.

No sub-issues, no linked issues, no activity and no attachment URLs. Each of
those would reach a second row, and the token grants exactly one.

`media` maps each attachment the body and comments embed to a media token bound
to this issue, so the reader's page can load the inline images and videos and
nothing filed under any other issue.
SharedIssue.title: SharedIssue

SharedIssueSummary.description: One row of a shared view's listing. The summary fields and nothing else.
SharedIssueSummary.title: SharedIssueSummary

SharedLabel.description: A label as a public reader sees it: its display, never its id.
SharedLabel.title: SharedLabel

SharedStatus.description: A status as a public reader sees it: its display, never its id.
SharedStatus.title: SharedStatus

SharedTarget.description:
What the first anonymous read answers: enough to render a heading.

No ids at all. The reader's client learns which of the two follow-up reads to
make and what to put in the page title, and nothing that is useful anywhere
else in the API.
SharedTarget.title: SharedTarget

SharedViewPage.description: A page of a shared view's issues, with the cursor for the next one.
SharedViewPage.title: SharedViewPage

StatusCreate.description:
The body a status create takes.

`color` and `icon` are optional, and a status without them renders from its
category. The icon must be one of its category's variants.
StatusCreate.title: StatusCreate

StatusListRead.description: The body the statuses list route answers with, ordered by position.
StatusListRead.title: StatusListRead

StatusRead.description: One workflow status as the API returns it, `null` color and icon meaning the default.
StatusRead.title: StatusRead

StatusUpdate.description:
The body a status patch takes.

An explicit null `color` or `icon` clears it back to the category default. The
icon is checked against the category in `team_workflow.update_status`, where
the stored category is known when the patch does not name one.
StatusUpdate.title: StatusUpdate

StorageUsageRead.description: The workspace's pooled attachment storage: what its uploads hold against its plan.
StorageUsageRead.title: StorageUsageRead

StripeWebhookAck.description: The acknowledgement returned to Stripe for a webhook delivery.
StripeWebhookAck.title: StripeWebhookAck

SubscriberRead.description: One person following the issue, named so the rail needs no second read.
SubscriberRead.title: SubscriberRead

SubscribersRead.description: Everyone following the issue, and whether the caller is one of them.
SubscribersRead.title: SubscribersRead

TeamListRead.description: The body the teams list route answers with.
TeamListRead.title: TeamListRead

TeamMemberListRead.description: The body the team members list route answers with.
TeamMemberListRead.title: TeamMemberListRead

TeamMemberRead.description: One team member, joined with their user row for display.
TeamMemberRead.title: TeamMemberRead

TeamMemberUpdate.description: The body a team membership put takes.
TeamMemberUpdate.title: TeamMemberUpdate

TeamRead.description: One team as the API returns it, carrying the caller's team role.
TeamRead.title: TeamRead

TeamSyncRead.description:
How one team's issues sync with one GitHub repository.

`two_way` carries changes both ways, `github_to_standupless` only imports and
follows GitHub, and `enabled` pauses both without forgetting the link.
TeamSyncRead.title: TeamSyncRead

TeamSyncWrite.description: Link a team to one repository, or change how it syncs.
TeamSyncWrite.title: TeamSyncWrite

TeamUpdate.description:
The body a team patch takes.

A new `key_prefix` retires the old one as an alias, so issue keys under the
old prefix keep resolving and no other team can take it.
TeamUpdate.title: TeamUpdate

TransitionCreate.description: Add a rule for a trigger and target branch pattern that has none.
TransitionCreate.title: TransitionCreate

TransitionRead.description:
One rule moving an issue when a pull request event happens.

`is_default` says the rule is not stored but computed from the design defaults,
so the frontend can show it as inherited rather than as something a person set.
`branch_pattern` is the glob the pull request's target branch must match, or
`None` for a rule that holds on any branch.
TransitionRead.title: TransitionRead

TransitionSet.description: A team's whole rule set, replacing whatever it had; empty restores the defaults.
TransitionSet.title: TransitionSet

TransitionUpdate.description: Repoint a rule at another status or none, or change the branch it holds on.
TransitionUpdate.title: TransitionUpdate

UploadCommit.description:
The body that records an uploaded object as an attachment.

Only this call makes an upload visible on the issue, so an abandoned one is an
orphaned object the lifecycle rule collects rather than a half-attached row.
UploadCommit.title: UploadCommit

UploadTicketCreate.description:
The body an upload ticket request takes.

`size_bytes` is what the client declares, and it becomes the `Content-Length`
signed into the URL, so S3 enforces the ceiling at the header rather than the
application measuring it after the bytes land.
UploadTicketCreate.title: UploadTicketCreate

UploadTicketRead.description:
The presigned PUT and the exact headers the client has to send.

`headers` comes straight from `PresignedUpload.headers` and none of it is
advisory: every header is inside the signature, so a PUT that omits or changes
one is refused by S3 rather than stored differently from what was authorised.
UploadTicketRead.title: UploadTicketRead

UrlAttachmentCreate.description: The body a URL attachment create takes.
UrlAttachmentCreate.title: UrlAttachmentCreate

UserPreferencesUpdate.description:
The preferences a person may change on their own account.

Both fields are optional, so the global email switch and one kind's channels
can each be changed without restating the other. Deliberately not a settings
domain of its own: a few values on the row the product already owns are cheaper
than a table and a second read on every notification.
UserPreferencesUpdate.title: UserPreferencesUpdate

UserRead.description: The caller's own account, in the shape the frontend's `UserRead` expects.
UserRead.title: UserRead

ValidationErrorDetail.description: One offending field in a 422, carrying its location and reason but never its input.

field.description: Dotted path to the offending field, or `_root` for the body itself.
field.title: Field

type.description: The pydantic error type, such as `missing` or `string_type`.
type.title: Type

ValidationErrorDetail.title: ValidationErrorDetail

VelocityCycleRead.description: One completed cycle's delivered work, frozen at its end date.
VelocityCycleRead.title: VelocityCycleRead

VelocityRead.title: VelocityRead

ViewCreate.description:
The body a saved view create takes.

`owner_id` and `scope` are absent on purpose: the owner comes from the
authorization context and the scope is derived from `team_id`, so neither is
something a caller can assert.
ViewCreate.title: ViewCreate

ViewListRead.description:
Every saved view a listing answers with.

No cursor: a member's own views and a team's views are both small by nature,
and a cursor would be a page boundary over two merged partitions.
ViewListRead.title: ViewListRead

ViewRead.description: One saved view as the API returns it.
ViewRead.title: ViewRead

ViewUpdate.description:
The body a saved view patch takes, every field optional.

`kind` and `team_id` are not patchable: the team decides the sort key the
row is filed under, so moving it would be a delete and a create wearing the name
of an update.
ViewUpdate.title: ViewUpdate

WebhookDeliveryRead.description:
One entry in a webhook's delivery log.

`request_body` is the JSON that was sent, cut to a preview when long, with
`request_truncated` saying so. `next_attempt_at` is set while a retry is queued.
WebhookDeliveryRead.title: WebhookDeliveryRead

WebhookEndpointCreate.description:
Register a webhook to deliver to.

`team_id` scopes it to one team; left out on the workspace route it covers every
team, and on a team route the path decides it.
WebhookEndpointCreate.title: WebhookEndpointCreate

WebhookEndpointRead.description:
One outbound webhook.

`secret` is populated only by the create and rotate calls. `secret_hint` is the
last four characters, which is enough for a person to tell two webhooks apart
without the value being recoverable from it. `team_id` is null for a webhook
that covers every team in the workspace. `disabled_reason` is set when repeated
failures turned the webhook off, which is the notice the settings page shows.
WebhookEndpointRead.title: WebhookEndpointRead

WebhookEndpointUpdate.description:
Change a webhook, leaving unset fields alone.

Turning `enabled` back on also clears a failure run and any auto-disable notice,
since re-enabling is the admin saying the receiver is fixed.
WebhookEndpointUpdate.title: WebhookEndpointUpdate

WorkspaceConnectedAppListRead.description: Every member grant in the workspace, most recently used first.
WorkspaceConnectedAppListRead.title: WorkspaceConnectedAppListRead

WorkspaceConnectedAppRead.description: One member's grant to one client in this workspace.
WorkspaceConnectedAppRead.title: WorkspaceConnectedAppRead

WorkspaceDeletionRequest.description:
The body `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/deletion` takes.

The workspace's name typed out again, compared exactly after trimming, so a
deletion is never one misplaced click.
WorkspaceDeletionRequest.title: WorkspaceDeletionRequest

WorkspaceRead.description:
One workspace as the API returns it.

`role` is the caller's own role, present only on a response to a member, so a
client can render the right controls without a second call.
WorkspaceRead.title: WorkspaceRead

WorkspaceSummaryRead.description: One workspace as the account deletion plan names it.
WorkspaceSummaryRead.title: WorkspaceSummaryRead

WorkspaceUpdate.description:
The body `PATCH /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}` takes.

Only the name is editable: the slug is the tenant's public handle and changing
one would break every link that carries it.
WorkspaceUpdate.title: WorkspaceUpdate

app__common__api__schemas__issues__Issue.description: One issue as the API returns it.
app__common__api__schemas__issues__Issue.title: IssueRead

app__domains__views__schemas__view__Issu.description: One issue as the board and the column route return it, the M2 shape.
app__domains__views__schemas__view__Issu.title: IssueRead

IdentityBearer.description: An identity access token, an MCP token or an API key, presented as a Bearer credential.

get.description: Whether this environment has an App yet, for the admin page to choose what to show.

404.description: The caller is not a platform admin, so the surface is not confirmed.

post.description: Exchange the manifest `code`, store the credentials, and answer only the id and slug.

404.description: The caller is not a platform admin, so the surface is not confirmed.

post.description: The manifest and signed state for one creation, refused when an App already exists.

404.description: The caller is not a platform admin, so the surface is not confirmed.

post.description:
Receive one Stripe event, answering 400 to anything unsigned or forged.

A missing signature is refused before the stage's billing state is consulted,
so the refusal is the same everywhere and the e2e suite can prove it.

400.description: The delivery is unsigned or its signature does not verify.

502.description: Stripe could not be reached while applying the event.

503.description: Billing is disabled or Stripe is not configured.

get.description:
Bind a finished GitHub install to the workspace whose admin started it.

GitHub sends the browser here with `installation_id`, `setup_action` and the
`state` the install url carried, either as the Setup URL or, with user
authorization during installation on, as the Callback URL with a `code` added.
The workspace comes from the signed state alone and never from a query
parameter, the state is redeemed once, and the installation id is checked
against GitHub with the App JWT before anything is written. A `code` is
exchanged only to ask GitHub whether the person who came back can reach the
installation: yes binds it even when it predates the state, no refuses it, and
no answer falls back to the freshness check. An `update` that GitHub sends with
no state, because the change started on GitHub, only refreshes an installation
that is already bound, and an install with no state, as when an organization
owner approves a member's request, binds nothing.

post.description:
Verify, claim and enqueue one GitHub delivery, then answer at once.

The order is the security property. The signature is checked over the raw body
before `json.loads` runs, so a forged delivery never reaches a parser. The
delivery id is then claimed in `idempotency`, which makes GitHub's redelivery
of a request whose response it never saw a no-op rather than a second set of
transitions.

get.description: Serve one team icon URL.
Serve one workspace logo or person avatar URL.

post.description:
Turn a token into a membership, idempotently for an existing member.

The token is looked up by hash, so no route in this product ever holds a
readable invite token. An expired or unknown token answers the same error, so
the response cannot tell one from the other.

delete.description:
End a session. Stateless here, so this only confirms the bearer.

Answered rather than refused because the specification has clients call it on
shutdown, and a 404 would make a clean disconnect look like a failure. There is
no server-side session to discard: every request carries its own bearer.

get.description:
Refuse a `GET`, carrying the challenge so discovery still starts from it.

405 rather than 404, because the path exists and the method does not. There is
no SSE stream to open here, which is what a client issuing a `GET` is asking
for.

post.description:
One JSON-RPC request or notification, answered in the response body.

The bearer is verified before the body is parsed, so an unauthenticated caller
never reaches the dispatch table and nothing it sends is acted on.

Resolving the bearer runs in a worker thread because verifying an OAuth token
fetches the issuer's key set over a blocking socket. On the event loop that call
stalls every other request on the worker, and where one process serves both the
issuer and this endpoint it stalls the very response it is waiting for, so the
fetch times out and a valid token reads as unverifiable.

get.description:
What one token resolves to, and the minimum needed to render a heading.

Loaded first by the public page so the client knows which of the two follow-up
reads to make. It answers names rather than ids, so learning that a token is
valid teaches nothing that can be spent on another route.

The one issue a token names, with its comments.

A token for a view answers the shared 404 rather than a 400, so the two kinds of
token are indistinguishable to someone probing with a guessed value.

One page of the issues a shared view or filter selects, inside its one team.

The team comes off the link rather than off the view, so a view edited to
point somewhere else after the link was minted still reads the team the
share was published against. That is what keeps a share's blast radius fixed at
the moment a person decided to publish it.

A saved view's link applies the view's live filter and sort, so the reader sees
what the view shows its team. A filter link replays the snapshot it was minted
with. Either way only issues the filter selects are listed, and a filter whose
team no longer agrees with the link's answers the 404 rather than widening.

The account behind the presented token or personal API key.

A personal key answers the person who minted it, which is how a command line
client learns who `me` is. A workspace key has no person and is a 403. A
verified token whose row is gone reads as 404 rather than 401, so the
frontend keeps the session and shows its unavailable state instead of
bouncing to login. A deleted account whose row the purge has not removed yet
is a 401.

delete.description: Remove the caller's avatar, falling back to their initials, and delete the image.

put.description: Make an uploaded image the caller's avatar and delete the one it replaces.

post.description: Sign a PUT for a new avatar image, which the commit call then makes current.

get.description: Every client the caller has authorized, grouped by client with a row per workspace.

delete.description:
Revoke the caller's grant to one client in every workspace.

A client the caller never authorized is a 404 rather than a silent success, so
the page can tell a stale row from a revocation that happened.

post.description:
Delete the caller's account now.

A signed in person only, with their address typed out again, and refused with a
409 naming each workspace where they are the only owner and other people remain.
Once it passes, the account is marked deleted, so no sign in method or refresh
works for it any more, then every session, OAuth grant and personal API key is
revoked and the purge of its data is started at once. The hourly sweep and the
queue's retries start any purge this request could not. The account's own
address is mailed, and the request is logged with how the caller last
authenticated. Repeating it for an account already deleted starts the purge again.

get.description: What deleting the caller's account would do, shown before they confirm it.

patch.description:
Change the caller's own preferences.

Separate from the identity package's own profile routes, which own the address
and the credentials; this owns the product fields on the same row, which is the
only part of it Standupless gets to define.

get.description:
Every workspace the caller is a member of, with their role on each.

Read through the memberships user index rather than an owner field, so a
member who does not own the workspace still sees it.

post.description:
Create a workspace and make the caller its first owner.

The membership is written after the workspace, because a workspace with no
owner is recoverable while an owner row pointing at nothing is not.

get.description: One workspace the caller belongs to, carrying their role and any scheduled deletion.

patch.description: Rename a workspace. The slug is fixed, so nothing else is editable.

get.description:
The caller's own keys, or every key in the workspace for an admin.

`mine` is the default rather than `workspace` so the ordinary read shows a
person only what they are responsible for, and widening it is a deliberate
query parameter that an admin check then has to pass.

post.description:
Mint a key and show its plaintext, the only time it is ever shown.

A workspace key acts as the synthetic principal `svc#<workspace_id>` rather
than as its minter, but it still only works while that minter is an owner or
admin of the workspace, so a departure or demotion disables it. Only an admin
may mint one because it acts for the workspace rather than for a person.

The limit is checked before the mint rather than enforced by a conditional
write, because the count spans the partition and no single-item condition can
express it. The race that leaves a workspace one key over is harmless: the
limit exists to stop unbounded growth, not to be exact.

delete.description:
Revoke one key the caller owns, or any key for a workspace admin.

A key the caller neither owns nor administers is a 404 rather than a 403, so a
member cannot walk key ids to learn what other people hold.

Revoking is idempotent: a key already revoked answers 204 rather than 404,
because the caller's intent is satisfied and a client retrying a revoke should
not have to distinguish the two.

get.description:
One page of an issue's attachments, oldest first.

No URL is minted here. A list of twenty attachments would otherwise be twenty
bearer credentials handed out whether or not anything is downloaded, so a URL
costs an explicit call for the one object the reader asked for.

post.description:
Record an uploaded object as an attachment, once it is really in the bucket.

The ticket is what proves the key was signed by this service for this caller on
this issue, so the recorded type and size are the ones S3 was told to enforce
rather than anything the commit body claims.

The object is checked for existence first, so a commit for an upload that never
happened is a 409 rather than a row pointing at nothing. Storage is checked again
here, because other uploads may have committed since the ticket was minted, and
the committed bytes are added to the workspace's counter.

get.description: Media tokens for every file attached to one issue the caller can see. The frontend appends each to the stable content path an inline image or video embeds, because an `` element carries no bearer token of its own. Visibility is decided here, once, and the token is what carries that decision to the content route.

post.description:
Mint a bounded presigned PUT, storing nothing on the issue yet.

The declared size is refused above the cap rather than quietly lowered, because
a client that declares 100 MB and receives a 25 MiB URL fails at the end of the
upload instead of the start. The same goes for the plan's pooled storage, which
the declared size is checked against before anything is signed.

The type is checked before signing rather than after the object lands: the type
goes into the signature, so refusing it here is what keeps the object from
existing at all.

Hang a link on an issue, deriving its favicon without fetching it.

The MVP does not crawl the target, so a title the caller does not give defaults
to the host and the favicon is a composed URL. Not fetching is the decision: a
crawl on a write path is a request the caller controls the destination of.

get.description: The workspace's pooled attachment storage, used against what its plan allows.

delete.description:
Detach one attachment, leaving its object to the bucket lifecycle rule.

The uploader or a team admin. The row is what makes an object visible on the
issue, so removing it is the whole of the delete a reader can observe, and the
object is collected by the bucket rather than by a delete this request has to
get right. The file's bytes are released from the workspace's storage at once.

get.description: Redirect to a fresh presigned GET for one embedded file, on a media token. The stable path is what a body stores; the token in the query is the credential, because an `` or `

Mint a short-lived presigned GET for one stored object.

The disposition is decided by the stored type, so anything outside the
inline-safe set downloads rather than rendering, and a stored `text/html` or
SVG cannot be served as a page from the bucket origin. The filename rides along
so a ULID key downloads under a human name.

The URL is a bearer credential for that one key until it expires. It is minted
per request and neither stored nor logged.

post.description:
Start a per-seat Stripe Checkout for a paid plan and return its URL.

A workspace that already holds a live subscription changes plan, interval or
payment method in the portal instead, so two subscriptions never bill at once.
Open the Stripe Customer Portal for the workspace's billing account.

get.description:
One team's whole board, a column per status in position order.

`cycle_id` and `project_id` are accepted because the contract fixes the query
signature, and they narrow nothing yet: an issue carries neither field until the
`planning` domain adds them, so filtering on one would be filtering on an
attribute no row has.
One board column, paged, for a column deeper than the board's own cap.

delete.description:
Remove one comment, reparenting its replies and dropping its reactions.

The author or a team admin. The replies are reparented to the thread root
rather than deleted with it, so removing a comment never takes someone else's
words with it, and the reactions go because nothing but this comment's id names
their partition.

get.description:
One comment the caller may read.

`issue_id` is required because it is the partition; without it this read would
be a scan, which the design forbids outside an admin path.

patch.description:
Rewrite one's own comment, stamping `edited_at` and re-extracting mentions.

The author alone, not a team admin: rewriting someone else's words is a
different act from removing them, and only the second has a moderation case.

Mentions are recomputed from the new body, so an edit that adds one notifies
and an edit that removes one stops claiming it.

get.description:
Every current member's grant in this workspace, for an admin.

Read one member at a time, because consents are indexed by person and not by
workspace. A grant held by someone no longer a member is not listed: their
token already fails at every route, which checks membership on each request.

delete.description:
Revoke one member's grant to one client in this workspace only.

Narrowed to this workspace's tenant, so an admin ends access to their own
workspace and never to another workspace the same person granted the client.

get.description:
One page of a team's cycles, by start date ascending.

The team is required rather than optional: a workspace-wide cycle list is
what the roadmap answers, and it answers it in date order across both entities
rather than as an undated pile of one of them.

The status filter is applied after the read because status is derived, so no
index can carry it.

post.description:
Create a cycle in one team.

Overlapping cycles are allowed: a team moving a cycle's dates would otherwise
have to delete and recreate it, and nothing downstream assumes an issue belongs
to at most one cycle in flight.

get.description:
A team's completed work over its last completed cycles, and the cycle to plan next.

Each cycle's figures are its value on its end date, so issues a cycle close
carried out the day after still count toward the scope it ended with and not
toward its completed work. Registered before the cycle id route so `velocity`
is never read as a cycle id.

delete.description:
Delete a cycle, leaving every issue that pointed at it in place.

The issues are not rewritten: an issue carrying a dead cycle id reads as
unassigned, and rewriting a team's whole issue set from a planning route
would be exactly the second write path the design forbids. The cycle's daily
snapshots go with it.

get.description: One cycle, or a 404 when the caller cannot see its team.

patch.description:
Patch a cycle's name, dates, goal or cancellation.

The row is read first and written whole, so the counters the consumer maintains
ride along untouched: a patch here must never become a second write path into
the numbers the stream owns.

get.description:
A cycle's daily scope, started and completed figures, from its first day on.

One value per day up to today or the cycle's end, whichever is sooner. A day
with no move of its own carries the previous day's value forward, and today
always reads the live counters.

delete.description: Cancel a scheduled deletion while the grace period lasts. Idempotent when none is scheduled.

post.description:
Schedule the workspace for permanent deletion after the grace period.

Owners and admins only, a signed in person only, and only with the workspace's
name typed out again. Repeating it keeps the first date. Every owner and admin
is mailed, and the request is logged with how the caller last authenticated.

get.description:
Where to send this admin to install the App on their GitHub account.

The state is minted per request and expires in minutes, so a url copied out of
a browser history is not a standing grant to bind an installation later.

delete.description:
Forget the installation and its repositories on this side.

This does not uninstall the App on GitHub, which only an account admin can do
there; the frontend links out for that. Webhook endpoints are deliberately left
alone, because they are a workspace's own outbound configuration and have
nothing to do with GitHub.

get.description:
The installation this workspace has, a 404 when it has none, or a 503 with no App.

The 503 is what lets the settings page say the environment has no App rather
than offering a connect button that can only fail.
Every repository the installation can see, with the team it feeds.

schema.title: Response List Repositories Api Workspaces  Workspace Id  Github Repositories Get

patch.description:
Point one repository at one team, or clear the link.

A repository with no team still receives events and still links issues, by
matching every team's prefix; naming a team narrows that to one prefix,
which is what a workspace with two teams sharing a number range wants.

delete.description: Remove the workspace logo, falling back to its initials, and delete the image.

put.description: Make an uploaded image the workspace logo and delete the one it replaces.

post.description: Sign a PUT for a new workspace logo, which the commit call then makes current.

get.description:
The caller's own notifications, newest first.

A notification whose issue or comment has since been deleted still renders,
carrying the title it was written with, rather than 404ing a whole list for one
stale row.

Snoozed notifications stay out of both lists until their time comes; `snoozed=true`
lists only them, and is refused beside `unread=true` since nothing is both.

How many of the caller's notifications are unread, capped at 100.

Capped because the badge stops meaning anything past that, and counting no
further keeps a busy inbox costing the same as a quiet one.

post.description:
Mark some or all of the caller's notifications read.

Ids that are already read, or that belong to someone else, count as nothing
changed rather than as an error: the write is conditional on the row being
unread in this caller's own partition, so a foreign id cannot be reached.

Hide some of the caller's notifications until a moment, when they return unread.

The moment must be at least a minute out and within the 90 day retention, so a
snooze can neither return before the request lands nor outlive the row.

Mark some of the caller's notifications unread again, ending any snooze.

Like mark-read, an id already unread or belonging to someone else counts as
nothing changed: the write is conditional on the row existing in this caller's
own partition, so a foreign id cannot be created or reached.

delete.description: Remove one of the caller's own notifications, or 404.

get.description: Every outstanding invite, without any token.

post.description:
Store an invite, mail it, and return its token exactly once.

Only the token's SHA-256 hash is stored, so this response is the only place
the token is readable. It is still returned after the mail goes out, because
the copy-link flow is what an admin falls back on when the address is one this
environment cannot reach, and a failed send never fails the invite.

delete.description: Revoke an invite before it is accepted.

get.description:
One page of the issues the caller may see, filtered and sorted.

Every id filter repeats, ORing its values, and `none` matches the unset field
where the field can be unset. Filters are applied after the key read rather
than through an index, so adding one costs no GSI. The cursor is a position in
the filtered, sorted set and is bound to the filter, so a cursor carried to a
different filter starts over rather than skipping rows.

The exception is a filter on one person: `subscriber_id=me`, one `creator_id`
or one `assignee_id` reads that person's own index instead of every team, which
is what the My issues tabs ask for. `subscriber_id` takes only the caller,
because what someone else follows is theirs to know.

Archived issues are left out unless `include_archived` is set, and
`archived_only` lists nothing but them, the archive view. That read goes
straight to each status's archived partition of the status index rather than
reading every issue of the team and dropping the live ones.

Every body carries `synced_at`. Sent back as `updated_since` with the same
filter, it turns the read into a delta: only the issues changed since, every
one in the list's sort order and unpaged, plus `removed_ids` for issues that
left the filter, were archived or were deleted. `resync_required` asks for a
full read instead, when the cursor is older than deletions are remembered or
the delta is too large to carry. A delta costs one key-bounded query per team
on the change feed index, so a poll that finds nothing reads almost nothing.

patch.description:
Apply one partial patch to up to `BULK_MAX_ISSUES` issues.

All or nothing on validation: every issue is loaded, authorized and has the
patch applied in memory before any is written, so an invisible issue (404), a
team the caller cannot write in (403) or a value one issue's team refuses (422)
fails the whole request with nothing changed. Each issue then goes through the
same write and activity path a single patch does, so history cannot tell a bulk
edit from one issue edited at a time. `archived` then archives or restores each
issue through the single-issue archive path, with the same team membership rule.

post.description:
Create an issue, allocating its key from the team's counter.

The counter is allocated after every validation has passed, because a number is
consumed whether or not the write lands and the contract accepts gaps but not
wasted ones.

get.description:
One issue by its human key, `ABC-123` and case insensitive.

Declared before `/issues/{issue_id}` so `by-key` is not swallowed as an id, and
the prefix names the team, which is what makes this one indexed query.

delete.description:
Delete an issue, reparenting its children and removing its links and history.

A team admin may always delete. Anyone else may delete only an issue they
created and only while it has no children, so an ordinary member cannot orphan
someone else's sub-issues.

get.description: One issue the caller may read.

patch.description:
Change an issue's fields and record one activity row per field that moved.

Activity is written here rather than by the stream consumer, so history can
name the actor: a stream record carries the change but not who made it.

get.description:
One page of an issue's history, newest first.

The sort key is a ULID, so descending order is the query's own direction and
the cursor is DynamoDB's start key rather than an offset into a merged set.

post.description:
Archive an issue, hiding it from lists and boards while keeping it searchable and restorable.

Idempotent: archiving an archived issue answers with it unchanged.

get.description: One page of an issue's direct children, oldest first.

One page of an issue's thread, oldest first so it reads in order.

Reply counts are computed over the whole thread rather than over the page,
because a reply can sit on a later page than its parent and a count of the page
alone would be wrong for every parent near a boundary.

post.description:
Add a comment to an issue, extracting its mentions on the way in.

A reply may only hang off a root comment: nesting past one level is a 409
rather than a silent reparent, because the contract makes `reply_count` a count
of direct replies and a deeper thread would make it a tree walk.

The inbox rows the mentions produce are written by the `views` notify consumer
off this table's stream, so the request path does no notification work. The
author and everyone mentioned are subscribed to the issue here, which is what
makes the next comment on it reach them.

Every named attachment must already be on this issue. The lookup is keyed by
the issue's own partition, so an id from another issue or workspace is refused
the same way as one that never existed.

get.description:
The pull requests that mention this issue, newest first.

The issue is loaded first so that an issue in a team the caller is outside
gives the same 404 as one that does not exist, rather than an empty list which
would confirm the id.

The GitHub issue this issue is synced with, or 404 when it has none.

An issue in a team the caller is outside gives the same 404 as one with no
link, so the answer confirms nothing about the id.

Every link touching one issue, in both directions.

The far sides are fetched in one batch so a page of links costs two calls
rather than one per row, and a link whose target the caller cannot see is left
out: the link is only meaningful if the issue it names is readable.

post.description:
Link two issues, idempotently on the same pair and type.

The caller must be able to write in the source's team and read the target's,
so a member of one team cannot attach an issue they merely know the id of.
A target they cannot see is a 404 rather than a 403, keeping ids unguessable.

delete.description:
Remove a link, both directions at once.

Named by `link_id` rather than by the pair, because the two rows share the id
and the caller holds it from the list; the inverse is then keyed off the stored
row instead of being reconstructed from the request.

get.description: Everyone following one issue the caller may read.

delete.description: Stop following the issue. Unsubscribing when not subscribed is not an error.

put.description: Follow the issue. Subscribing twice keeps the first subscription.

post.description:
Restore an archived issue to its lists and board.

Idempotent: restoring a live issue answers with it unchanged.

get.description: Everyone in the workspace, joined with their user rows for display.

delete.description:
Remove a member, or leave the workspace yourself.

Declared at read level because leaving is something any member may do; an
admin removing someone else is checked here instead of by the capability.

patch.description:
Change a member's workspace role.

Only an owner may grant or remove ownership, and the last owner cannot be
demoted, which is the same invariant that stops them being removed.

get.description:
One page of the workspace's projects the caller can see, by target date, undated last.

A project is listed when the caller can see at least one of its teams, and
`team_id` narrows to the projects that team is on. The rows are read whole
and paged over the filtered order, so a page is never left short by projects
the caller cannot see. Undated projects sort last, because an absent target is
a project nobody has committed to yet.

post.description:
Create a project on one or more teams.

The caller must be able to write in every team named, since a project put on a
team appears in that team's planning.

delete.description:
Delete a project and its milestones, leaving every issue that pointed at it in place.

Takes an administrator of every one of the project's teams, because the
delete detaches issues in each of them.

get.description: One project, or a 404 when the caller can see none of its teams.

patch.description:
Patch a project's fields or its teams.

Any writer on one of the project's visible teams may edit its fields. Changing
`team_ids` also needs write access to every team added or removed. Setting a
date, the lead or the description to null clears it. The row is read first and
written whole, so the counters the consumer maintains ride along untouched.

get.description:
Every milestone of one project, in its manual order, with progress counts.

A project holds a bounded set, so the list is answered whole and never pages.

post.description: Add a milestone to a project, after the last one unless a position is given.

delete.description:
Delete one milestone; its issues stay in the project with no milestone.

Takes the same right as editing the project, since it removes a stage of the
plan rather than any team's work.

patch.description:
Rename, redate, redescribe or reorder one milestone.

The row is read first and written whole, so the counters the rollup consumer
maintains ride along untouched.

get.description: One page of a project's updates, newest first.

post.description: Post an update, which sets the project's health to the one it reports.

delete.description: Delete an update, as its author or an admin.

patch.description: Edit an update's body or health, as its author or an admin.

delete.description:
Take back one's own reaction, whether or not it was there.

The reacting user alone: the key names them, so there is no route by which one
member removes another's reaction. Removing one that is absent is still 204,
because the caller's intent is already satisfied.

The emoji is normalised the way the write normalised it, so a client sending
the variation selector form removes the row it created rather than missing it.

get.description:
Every reaction on one target, grouped by emoji.

Not paged: a group is a count over the whole partition, so a page boundary
would hand back a count of part of it.

put.description:
React to a target, answering with that emoji's group as it now stands.

Idempotent by key, so a second PUT by the same user is the same row and the
same answer rather than a conflict. Only that emoji's group comes back, because
that is the one the caller just changed and the rest are already on screen.

get.description:
One page of the workspace's roadmap, by date ascending, undated last.

The read fans out one index query per readable team for cycles, reads the
workspace's projects once, and merges, so the cursor is a position in the merged
order rather than a start key: a merged page has no single last evaluated key.
A team the caller is outside is never queried, and a project on no team the
caller can see is dropped before the merge, so neither can influence a page
boundary.
Ranked search hits, by matched term count and then by recency.

Every share link the caller may see, newest first.

Narrowed to one target when both query parameters arrive, which is what an
issue page asks for. Without them the answer is every link onto every issue and
view of the teams this caller can read, so a guest sees only the teams
they hold a membership in.

post.description:
Mint a share link onto one issue, one view or one team filter, and show its token once.

The team and the title are resolved from the target row and denormalised
onto the link, so a settings listing needs no second read and the anonymous
read is bounded by a team id that was decided at create time rather than
re-derived later against whatever the row says then.

delete.description:
Revoke one link the caller created, or any link for a team admin.

Named by hash rather than by token, because the settings list is what a person
revokes from and the token is deliberately the one thing that list does not
carry.

A link in a workspace the caller is not in, or onto a team they cannot see,
answers the same 404 an absent one does, so the hash space cannot be probed.

get.description:
Every team in the workspace the caller may see.

A guest sees only the teams they are a member of, which is the same rule
the single team route applies, read off the context rather than repeated.

post.description:
Create a team, make the caller its admin and seed the default statuses.

All three land as one `TransactWriteItems` across the three tables, seven items
in total, because a team written without its statuses is unusable and cannot
be recreated: the prefix is taken, so a retry 409s while issue creation 422s on
the missing statuses. All or nothing means a failure leaves the prefix free.

delete.description:
Delete a team: tombstone it, then purge the rows this domain owns.

The tombstone hides the team from every read and frees its key prefix before
anything else goes, so a crash part way leaves a hidden team a retry resumes,
never a visible half-deleted one. Memberships, statuses, labels, transitions,
the issue counter and retired prefix aliases are purged a page at a time.
The rows other domains own (issues, comments, cycles, views, GitHub links)
are handed to the team purge chain, whose last stage removes the tombstoned
row. Without the chain's queues the tombstone simply stays. A repeat call on
a team that is gone answers 204 again, and one on a team still deleting
starts the chain again, which is how a purge parked in a dead-letter queue
is resumed.

get.description: One team the caller may read, with its member count and retired prefixes.

patch.description:
Change a team's name, key prefix, description or estimate scale.

A new key prefix is applied first, in its own transaction, so a 409 on a
taken prefix leaves every other field of the patch unapplied too.

get.description: A team's auto-archive period, the six month default when none was saved.

patch.description:
Change after how many months a team's completed and cancelled issues are archived.

The hourly sweep reads the new period on its next run, so a shorter period
archives the newly due issues within the hour rather than at once.

get.description: A team's automatic cycle settings, the defaults when none were saved.

patch.description:
Change a team's automatic cycle settings.

When cycles are on after the change, the team's missing current and upcoming
cycles are created before the response, so the cycles page shows them at
once rather than after the next hourly run. Turning cycles off keeps every
cycle already created.

delete.description: Stop syncing this team. Issues already imported stay, and stop following GitHub.

get.description: The repository this team's issues sync with, or 404 when there is none.

put.description:
Link this team to a repository the installation can see, or change the link.

A repository already syncing with another team is refused with 409, because
one GitHub issue cannot belong to two teams. Only issues opened after the link
are imported; existing ones stay on GitHub.

Saving an enabled link also queues a backlink job for each synced issue whose
backlink comment is missing or out of date, so saving the settings again is
how a team admin backfills backlinks or refreshes them after a prefix rename.

get.description: What this team actually does on each pull request event.

schema.title: Response List Transitions Api Workspaces  Workspace Id  Teams  Team Id  Github Transitions Get

post.description: Add the rule for one trigger and branch pattern, which must not already have one.

put.description: Replace the team's whole rule set, an empty list restoring the defaults.

schema.title: Response Replace Transitions Api Workspaces  Workspace Id  Teams  Team Id  Github Transitions Put

delete.description: Remove one rule. Removing the last one restores the defaults.

patch.description: Repoint one rule at another status or at none, or change its branch pattern.

delete.description: Remove the team icon, falling back to its initials, and delete the image.

put.description: Make an uploaded image the team icon and delete the one it replaces.

post.description: Sign a PUT for a new team icon, which the commit call then makes current.

Join a team as a member, or answer the membership already held unchanged.

Every team is open to a workspace member. A guest reaches only the teams an
admin added them to, so for a guest this never widens access.

get.description: Every label of the team, in name order.

post.description: Add a label to the team.

delete.description: Delete a label.

patch.description: Rename or recolour a label.

post.description: Leave a team. The last admin must hand the role on first.

get.description: Everyone explicitly added to this team, joined with their user rows.

delete.description: Remove someone from the team. A guest loses access to it entirely.

put.description:
Add someone to the team, or change the role they already hold.

Only an existing workspace member can be added, because a team membership
is a narrowing of workspace access and never a grant of it.

get.description: Every status of the team, ordered by position.

post.description: Add a status, defaulting its position to the end of the list.

delete.description:
Delete a status, refusing the last one of its category.

The board renders a column per category, so removing the only status of one
would leave a category that can be assigned but never displayed.

patch.description: Rename a status, recategorise it or move it in the order.

get.description: The webhooks scoped to one team.

schema.title: Response List Team Webhooks Api Workspaces  Workspace Id  Teams  Team Id  Webhooks Get

post.description: Register a webhook for one team.

delete.description: Delete one of a team's webhooks.

patch.description: Change one of a team's webhooks.

get.description: The delivery log of one of a team's webhooks.

schema.title: Response List Team Webhook Deliveries Api Workspaces  Workspace Id  Teams  Team Id  Webhooks  Webhook Id  Deliveries Get

post.description: Redeliver one logged delivery of one of a team's webhooks.
Send a test ping to one of a team's webhooks.
Mint a new secret for one of a team's webhooks.

get.description:
Saved views the caller may read, narrowed by scope.

`all` is the caller's own views plus the team views of teams they can see,
which for a guest is only the teams they hold a membership in, so the listing
is built from what they may read rather than filtered afterwards.

post.description:
Save a new view, personal unless it names a team.

A team view needs the caller to be a member of that team: a reader could
otherwise leave a shared view on a team they cannot write in.

delete.description: Remove a saved view, the owner's or a team admin's call.

get.description: One saved view the caller may read, or a 404.

patch.description:
Change a saved view's name, filter, sort, grouping or display settings.

The display switches take true or false and never null, because a switch
that could be neither would leave the client guessing what the view shows.

get.description: Every webhook in the workspace, team scoped ones included, without any secret.

schema.title: Response List Webhooks Api Workspaces  Workspace Id  Webhooks Get

post.description: Register a webhook for every team, or for the team named in the body.

delete.description: Delete any webhook in the workspace.

patch.description: Change any webhook in the workspace.

get.description: The delivery log of any webhook in the workspace.

schema.title: Response List Webhook Deliveries Api Workspaces  Workspace Id  Webhooks  Webhook Id  Deliveries Get

post.description: Redeliver one logged delivery of any webhook in the workspace.
Send a test ping to any webhook in the workspace.
Mint a new secret for any webhook in the workspace.
